The matching paper is GraphER: An Efficient Graph-Based Enrichment and Reranking Method for Retrieval-Augmented Generation by Ruizhong Miao, Yuying Wang, Rongguang Wang, and coauthors [1]. It proposes a graph-based enrichment and reranking framework for RAG that builds a graph at query time from proximity relationships in the data, then applies graph-based ranking to surface top candidate documents [1]. The paper emphasizes improved retrieval completeness across table retrieval, multi-hop retrieval, and long-document retrieval, while requiring no additional graph infrastructure and integrating with standard vector stores [1].

Related reranking papers differ in how they use graphs. L2G also supports graph-based retrieval, but it induces document graphs from listwise reranker logs instead of constructing a query-time graph like GraphER [2]. Other RAG reranking work here focuses on utility-aligned reranking with LLM feedback or efficient listwise reranking rather than graph-based enrichment, such as RRPO and LURE-RAG [3,4].
